finding.guards_checked: Only a balance check exists. Compare /withdraw at line 21, which has amount <= 0; transfer lacks it. No type check (strings or floats), no recipient existence check, no self-transfer check.

verdict.guard_found: Only the balance check `BAL[g.user] < amount` (bank.py:11), which a negative amount passes. No sign or type check. No before_request or auth hook exists in the codebase, and g.user is never set.
verdict.reason: bank.py:11 only tests `BAL[g.user] < amount`, so a negative amount passes. Lines 13-14 then subtract from the sender and add to the victim, which moves funds from the victim to the attacker. /withdraw has the `amount <= 0` guard at bank.py:21 and /transfer does not. The attacker only needs to be any user who can reach the endpoint.

finding.claim: No authentication is implemented, and g.user is never set in this file. No before_request or auth hook exists. If a hook elsewhere is absent, requests fail; if g.user is later populated from an untrusted source, there is no verification here. The code relies on an assumed external control. Also, balances are mutated with no locking, so concurrent requests can double-spend (check-then-act race at lines 11-13 and 21-23).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST requests; concurrent requests
finding.sink: BAL balance mutations at lines 13-14 and 23

finding.guards_checked: Searched the only file in the repository (bank.py) for before_request, auth decorators, g.user assignment, and locks. None found. The race is only exploitable under a threaded or multi-worker server, and BAL is in-process memory.

verdict.guard_found: none (no before_request, auth decorator, g.user assignment, or lock; bank.py is the only file)
verdict.reason: The check-then-act race is real: bank.py:11 reads BAL[g.user] and bank.py:13 decrements it with no lock (same pattern at bank.py:21 and 23), so concurrent requests can both pass the check. Two caveats: g.user is never set anywhere, so as written every request raises AttributeError, and the unauthenticated-access claim depends on code that isn't in this repo. Also, bank.py:11-14 never checks amount <= 0, so a negative transfer amount would pull funds from the recipient.
